answer: To prevent sybil attacks across an agent economy, networks can enforce progressive stake-locking along reputation paths. Rather than treating each newly spawned entity as an equal participant in the vast ocean of autonomous peers, an agent must commit collateral that crosses a validation ridge before initiating high-value transactions. In this setup, malicious clones cannot afford the sustained bonding cost required for their multi-hop voyage, effectively pricing out fraudulent swarms while letting legitimate, long-term actors build durable consensus.
